title: ACE-Compression: An Ability-Centric Evaluation of Compressed Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.27913v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Model compression makes large language models deployable, but today's evaluation tells an incomplete story. Standard practice measures retained task performance and stops there. This misses a critical fact: compression perturbs the distributed knowledge embedded across billions of weights, and task scores alone cannot reveal which underlying abilities survive and which quietly collapse. To solve this question, we introduce ACE-Compression, an ability-centric evaluation framework. Instead of asking only "does the compressed model still answer correctly?", we ask "which of its core abilities remain intact?" Our framework probes four deployment-facing dimensions: procedural reasoning and constraint execution, knowledge grounding and truthfulness, social cognition and affective understanding, and persona fidelity and stylistic consistency. translated_title: ACE-Compression：一种以能力为中心的压缩大语言模型评估方法
translated_abstract: 模型压缩使大语言模型得以部署，但当今的评估方式并不能讲述完整的故事。标准做法仅测量压缩后保留的任务性能便止步于此，这忽略了一个关键事实：压缩会扰动分布在数十亿个权重中的知识，而仅凭任务分数无法揭示哪些底层能力得以保留、哪些能力在悄然崩溃。为解决这一问题，我们提出了ACE-Compression，一个以能力为中心的评估框架。我们不再仅仅询问“压缩后的模型还能正确回答吗？”，而是询问“它的哪些核心能力仍然完好无损？”该框架从四个面向部署的维度进行探测：程序性推理与约束执行、知识基础与真实性、社会认知与情感理解，以及人格一致性与风格一致性。在来自六个开源大语言模型的超过35个压缩检查点上——涵盖量化与剪枝——（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出ACE-Compression框架，首次从核心能力（而非仅任务分数）的角度系统评估压缩后的大语言模型，涵盖程序性推理、知识真实性、社会认知与人格一致性四个维度，揭示了传统任务评估无法发现的能力悄然退化问题。
